dialogue.text: insightful and sharp. A masterful spin through the tortured human psyche. That's Lorrie Moore. wise and deeply empathetic... Amy bloom. I guess... I guess it's good.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: How does it feel, reading those quotes? That's high praise for a woman whose talent and intellect You say you respect. And yet you read that...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'm happy for her. I am. I am. - Okay. See, I'm not claiming that it's not... it's not complicated, There's not some... Jealousy. Sure, but... of course. I should... well, I should wait till I read it myself. But... but I uh... I am pleased for her, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What are you jealous of?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, clearly she's made a new life for herself, Found a way to escape from... From patients like me. Quite a feat really... phoenix like.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Why are you so convinced Gina wanted to escape from you?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Give me another 10 minutes and you'll understand completely.

situation: I talk about discussing patient feelings with Gina, who found it repulsive, sparking the doctor's curiosity.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Give me another 10 minutes and you'll understand completely. You're probably feeling it already.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: No. I hadn't been.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, you're extremely polite.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you feel that way with your patients, like you want to escape?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You know, I told Gina once That with patients I feel like... It's like two mice in a glue trap... Stuck, immobile, Getting nowhere. She was disgusted to hear that.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you still feel that way?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I've been a therapist for... For 25 years, you know? Really, you couldn't possibly, But you will.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Oppressive. Oppressive. You start to see the limitations, The artifice of it all.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: In what ways? I'm genuinely curious. Another analyst across from me... I'd really like to know what your experience has been. I'd... I... I'd like to know what's coming.

situation: I discuss my feelings when treating Jesse.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I see this teenager, Jesse. He's 16, Adopted, gay, Aggressive... pushes everybody away. Anyway, his, um... His birth mother called him this week Just out of the blue. And he hasn't been able to tell anybody... not his mother,

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: but he told you?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah. He told me. It paid to listen intently. There are times in that room where I feel... I really feel that we connect, We make contact. And then he goes back into the world... The real world, the actual world... And he just... He implodes And the work that we've done together is just... It's just gone.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I recognize that feeling. It's incredibly frustrating To feel like you're not making progress. - Mm-hmm. But don't you think even t act of listening has value?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I've been seeing this new patient...

situation: I talk about treating Sunil.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I've been seeing this new patient... An immigrant from Calcutta. He wife died about six months ago. So his son and his daughter-in-law Have him stuck in the spare room... No friends, no one to talk to. So they drag him to see me To make everything better. And all he wants from me... All he wants from me Is for me to bring his wife back. He's got the loneliest face I've ever... I've ever seen. Hmm. Sits across from me looking trapped, Without an ounce of belief that I can do anything to help him. And sometimes I just wanna say, Sunil, you' right. There's-there's nothing I can do.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You described both of these patients As not having someone to talk to, confide in... At least outside your office. And I'm wondering if you do.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: If I... if-if I...

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: The therapist asks if I have anyone to talk to, I mention Wendy.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: If I... if-if I... If I do what?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: All the significant attachments in your life... The ones you've mentioned here... Your father, your wife, Gina... have ended. You say you're seeing less of your kids. I mean, do you have someone... a friend, A companion, another adult... to talk to? You mentioned you were college friends With Dr. Burdick who referred you here.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Do-do I, uh... No. But we're not really friends. We're more old ac Clientuaintances. But yes, I do have somebody to talk to. I've... her name is Wendy. We've been seeing each other. And yeah, I talk with her. We... We talk.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Is that who you were on the phone with in the waiting room? Yes. - You told her you were somewhere else. What was it, the grocery store?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, she's 37. I'm 57. I-I haven't gotten to the place Where I feel comfortable telling her I have Parkinson's.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, I can understand your not wanting to tell your girlfriend About the possibility of having Parkinson's, But letting her know you have a therapy appointment Isn't exactly the same thing. You're not seeing me for Parkinson's.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, I mean, it... it's all related, isn't it?

situation: I ask for medication.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: And because? I'm having the dream, Ase, I can't sleep.He dream. And because I can't sleep, I'm here... About to be late for a movie, Waiting for you to write a prescription.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Understood.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You and Wendy?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes, Wendy and me.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm gonna prescribe the extended-release tablets. Some people find them helpful in sleeping through the night.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Thank you. Just remember...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You can't take more until six hours have elapsed. How was your sleep last night?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I woke up at 2:30 And couldn't get back asleep.

situation: The therapist tries to interpret my dream.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I woke up at 2:30 And couldn't get back asleep. Mm-hmm.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You used very similar language when you spoke Both about the possibility of having Parkinson's As well as your experience of being a therapist. You talked about Sunil being stuck up in the spare room, About feeling trapped like mice in a glue trap with your patients. That same language of escape and entrapment Came up when you spoke about Gina. I'm wondering if your dream has similar imagery.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No. Actually, it doesn't. Thank you for this.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: May I ask you one last thing?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You said you had the dream again last night?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Here's what confuses me... If you figured out several days ago what the dream means, The content has be communicated from your unconscious To your conscious mind. Why are you still having it?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I've gotta go.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Enjoy your movie.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: If you decide you wanna talk any further, My door is always open to you.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: What did you just say?

situation: I talk about being splashed with soda on a train.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Did this happen on the train?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I have to travel only three stops, But I guess this is what happens in America.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You're okay?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'll survive, Dr. Weston. It is only mountain dew.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And did these kids... did they... Did they apologize to you?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I do not think they noticed.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That's a lot of soda not to notice. Did you say anything to them?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: What good that would do? Besides, they cannot hear anyway. They are all wearing little headphones.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You're very forgiving. I'm sorry about your train ride. Well, I'm glad that you're here. Can I ask you how...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: How things are at home?

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I talk about my family asking me to take a bath.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: How things are at home? They begged me to take a shower.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Your son and your daughter-in-law?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: All four of them knocked on my door this morning. They made Naya ask me. She says, grandpa, please take a shower.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So how did that make you feel...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Being asked to bathe by your granddaughter? I must admit I was starting to smell like a goat.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So they got your notebook as well?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, I was using it on the train, so...

situation: I hope the therapist can cure my pain.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: It's not so wet. Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: May I?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She's beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Is... was this on your wedding day?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Just after the ceremony.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Are you... Are you okay, Mr. Sanyal?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I am only tired. Recently I have not been sleeping so well. I wake with... With... with an ache.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What kind of ache?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I suppose it is this ailment That my son hopes you will relieve me of. You and I will speak and my pain will heal Like a fractured bone.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I wish it was that simple. If it's any comfort to you, I agree with what you said at our last session. I don't think that grief has any schedule. And I have no desire To speed up your grieving process.

situation: I propose a logic game, the therapist says therapy is different.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You are not married?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What makes you ask that?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Last time when I asked, you said, no, I don't have a wife.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That's true. Yes, I did.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Are we playing a logic game? You are also a widower then? Forgive me. You know, where I'm from, When we want to talk, We meet a friend for tea. And then one person speaks and then the other. It is very strange to be expected To do all the talking continuously, you know.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I understand, but... but this is... This is what therapy is. It's... it's... it's... Well, it's not exactly the same As meeting a friend for tea.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You said last week we could simply have a conversation. That's true. I did say that. And during the conversation You scarcely said a word. I am expected to disclose the details of my life,

situation: I talk about my marriage, thinking the pattern was good for me.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I am expected to disclose the details of my life, To speak about my wife, About my pain, about... Or share her photograph or, you know...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I did have a wife. But... We're divorced now.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: How long 21 years. Were you married? Do you miss her?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Sometimes I... Yes, I do.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: In Hinduism, when... When the wife dies before the husband, Before she is cremated, She is dressed in her red bridal clothes. And now when I see her wedding photo I think of her funeral. She used to tease me That in our wedding photo I look like I'm entering into a pool Containing a giant octopus. We were both still very young. And like most brahmin marriages, It was arranged. I'd just graduated from the university. She and her family came over to our home. There was a short interview Which lasted perhaps two hours. And our parents decided That we were to be married shortly after that. This was going to be my future. And when your future walks into the room And sits beside you on the carpet, It could be, you know, Quite disconcerting. These things work differently in America.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, they are different, yes. But whether they work is another question. In some ways An arranged marriage seems like it might be simpler.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I would say for us it was fine.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Only... only fine?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Fine... fine is good. Yeah, perhaps... Perhaps she was my closest friend.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: How often do you find yourself Thinking about kamala?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Many many times each day.

situation: My wife would not agree with the daughter-in-law's parenting style.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Many many times each day. I often think of her when I see Julia.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So... So when you see Julia, You're reminded of... of your wife? Of the differences between them.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: It's... it's impossible not to. Look, kamala would not have approved Of the way Julia is raising our grandchildren. What do you mean? Why wouldn't she approve? She might think that they're spoiled, That there's too little discipline. She might think the minute they don't get what they want They scream, they throw tantrums. And do you think that's true? Our son was raised differently. Kamala taught him Good manners, humility, Because it was important to her.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And it sounds like it's important to you. Would you say that's true?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Can I ask you What else is in your notebook? Many things. Sometimes I write to kamala too. In your notebook? Yeah, very simple things. Like... Like hello, Good morning, good night, Or the sun is very hot today, Or the birds are too loud for sleeping. Things like this.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Have you ever written to her about your grandchildren?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I tell her that she would be Quite fond of them.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you share your concerns with kamala About how Julia Is raising your grandchildren?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: So can I smoke?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yeah, sure. You can smoke, yes.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I talk about encountering my daughter-in-law while bathing, she mocks me.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Dr. Weston, please call me Sunil.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Okay. And you must call me Paul.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Mm-hmm, Paul. You know what happened this morning? A plumber came to fix my shower, So I had to use Arun and Julia's bathroom. As I was coming out of the shower... Julia came in. I had the towel wrapped around my waist. She entered just as I was putting A small piece of soap in a dish On top of the toilet tank... A little purple soap goose That smelled of lavender. She was preparing to take the shower too. So she was also in her towel? She very quickly covered herself with her towel, yes. She froze. She obviously forgot about the plumber.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And what happened?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I said, excuse me And then went up to my room to get dressed. 10 minutes later she knocked on my door.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What did she say?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She became very angry. She spoke to me as if I'm a child... Because of soap.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, she'd just been confronted by the fact That you're not a child at all. She may have been covering for other feelings That she had from seeing you in this way. What feelings?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: My daughter-in-law is not A modest woman, I assure you.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I describe my feelings when encountering my daughter-in-law in the bath.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: My daughter-in-law is not A modest woman, I assure you. She still showers with Sam even though he's nearly six. For her it's perfectly appropriate.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: But not to you.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You are the expert. Please tell me. Where was your son when all of this happened? He had already left for work. Sunil, when Julia was here last week, She mentioned feeling Uncomfortable at times Because of the way that you look at her. Would you say that this encounter In the bathroom Might have been one of those moments? We were both in our towels, Paul. And I said, excuse me. And I went out.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, I understand that. What I'm asking is... Can you say a bit more about how you felt When your daughter-in-law surprised you?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I would say I felt surprised.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, but what else?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I said to myself, see, here's your daughter-in-law, And she is wearing a towel. I don't understand the rules of this house.

situation: I say my son has become like his daughter-in-law.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: My son and Julia are very different people. I used to believe That these differences were what drew him to her, Beyond her yellow shining hair.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And you don't think that anymore?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Now the differences are less and less. He has become more like her, As if under a spell. I wonder how he feels not being The master of his own house. That's how you see... you see Arun? He prepares her cappuccino for her every morning, And precisely as she wishes too... With just the right amount of steamed skim milk And one cube of organic brown sugar. He puts the dishes away in the cupboard, Gives the children their evening bath So that she can read in her study.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Maybe your son enjoys these activities... That he makes Julia her cappuccino in the morning And puts the dishes away because... Because he wants to. I'm not... I'm not for a moment dismissing your concerns. I think you have very legitimate concerns. But I do think it's possible They may be yours more than his. You're dealing with very real frustrations, Yet most of your complaints Your son must be unhappy; Your grandchildren's upbringing would disappoint kamala; Kamala would disapprove of Julia. I guess I'm beginning to wonder If you have trouble voicing Grievances of your own. The fact of the matter is that you're the one Who feels stuck in your son's house, Who's been cloistered away upstairs with the kids. They knocked on your door this morning To make a collective request about your hygiene. Julia polices the way you handle the objects in her bathroom. You don't have the power to smoke where or when you want. You have a right to be angry. And it's becoming clear to me That on some level you are. So I'm just thinking it might be helpful To everybody, but mostly for you If you could begin to express that anger More directly, try to put it into... Try to put it into words.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: The therapist says I have the right to express my demands.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'm beginning to regret That I requested you to speak more. This is not quite what I'd meant By balanced conversation.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I know. You'd rather meet a friend for tea.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Tea is terrible in New York. You disagree?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Oh no, I don't.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You're Irish. You must enjoy tea.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, I do.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: So maybe you can tell me what is wrong with Americans. In India we drink hot tea. Here it is often no warmer than dishwater.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That's true.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See? There, I was expressing my frustration. How did I do?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It's a good start.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I talk about conflicts that arose the first time my daughter-in-law came to our house.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See, there was one occasion When I spoke openly to Arun, When I presented my displeasure.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And when was that?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Many years ago, when he and Julia were first engaged. We had never met Julia. So they came to Calcutta to tell us the good news.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You didn't see it that way?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: At first I did. Arun seemed so happy, Like a small child handed a special dessert, Barely able to breathe. I must admit I was pleased For arun to receive so much attention, Much more than we were used to seeing... Like holding hands, sitting very close. She... she even curled his hair behind his ear, eh? In our presence. I thought kamala was going to faint.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And how did things go between kamala and Julia?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Very bad. Mm-hmm. Toward the end of dinner Julia expressed her disappointment That we would not allow her to stay at our home.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So where was she staying?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: In a hotel.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And where was arun?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: He stayed with us, in his old room. You must understand It's not acceptable For a couple to sleep In the House of the parents before they are married. So during dinner it was clear She wanted arun to discuss these matters with us. So when arun could not bring himself to do it, She proceeded to do so herself. She said they had traveled such a far distance And they are very tired And they wished not to be separated. Arun was so embarrassed, He could not even look at his mother and me.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: How did you and your wife respond to that?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: After arun left to escort Julia back to her hotel, Kamala was so angry, She could not speak for more than one hour. Then she pleaded with me to speak to arun.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I discuss talking to my son about the daughter-in-law, my son attacks me fiercely.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: So the next night, I sat in the kitchen with arun And asked him whether he... Whether he was sure about his decision to marry.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What did he say?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: He lashed out at me. He said we did not approve of Julia Because... because she's not Bengali. And he said I could not relate to his life And I married a woman I did not love And I... I chose duty over passion And... and... And I'm jealous. So they cut their visit short by three days And left to America the following morning.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So do you think there was any truth in what arun said?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: That I do not know passion?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: He also said that you were jealous.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I talk about my wife asking our son to promise to take care of me on her deathbed.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Perhaps I did not marry For the same reasons as my son, But I came to love my wife.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Did you ever wish for something more in life? Do you wish for something more?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: After that, Things were different with arun. When Samuel was born we came to New York, And again after Naya. But it was never the same.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Did arun ever come back to Calcutta to visit?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Only once, When his mother was in serious decline, Just two days before she passed.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That must have been another difficult visit. What were you just thinking?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: On this same visit my son made his promise to kamala.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That he would bring you back to New York.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes, she told him that I was not capable of living on my own And he must take care of me always. These were the last words she spoke.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And so here you are.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Here I am.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you wish you had stayed in Calcutta?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See, it is the way we do things, Paul... The children care for their parents.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you think about going back?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: It's not possible.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Why not?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I have no money, Paul.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I talk about being unable to leave, my money went towards my son's education and my wife's treatment.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I have no money, Paul. Although I should have, but I do not.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Can I ask you why not?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See, much of my earnings went toward paying For Arun's American education. And what was left was spent On kamala's medical bills. So... There is nothing to be done.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You seem resigned. Have you and your son ever discussed

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: The fight that you had on that first visit? We have never spoken of it... Never.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm... I'm afraid our time is up, sunil.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm supposed to leave?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I have another patient, But we can pick up here the next week.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Okay okay. If I'm going to walk, How do I get to prospect park?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Prospect park? That's easy. You go out, you turn left, Pass the coffee shop on the corner, Across the main drag. Once you...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'll find it. I'll find it. No problem. Okay. No problem.

situation: I tell what happened during the week.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You look tired. I'm sorry. I hate that. Don't ever tell me when I look like shit or tired... Or old.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What's that?

situation: I talk about a dream I had and I was scared.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Will you tell me what you've been dreaming?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'm... I'm running Along the outside of this Tall wrought-iron fence. I'm outside. It's a field, Daytime, really bright. The fence starts to curve And I can sense This opening up ahead... Gates. And I have this tremendous feeling of excitement. My heart is thumping. I have this anticipation. And then My legs just... They get... they get heavy And I'm slowing down As if I'm stuck in quicksand. And I can't move. I sense something behind me. And I turn my head. And... It's my father. He's walking towards me. I'm paralyzed. He's coming closer. And he's lurching Towards me. And... And then I wake up with a start. I just startle awake.

situation: I talk about becoming a father.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I've been having that dream for months, Since just after the symptoms started. I... Think I'm becoming my father. I'm being overtaken by him. I've tried my best to ignore it... The symptoms of the disease, The coming paralysis. Then I have the dream again And it's... it's clear to me What it's communicating. I just can't... I can't ignore it anymore. I woke up the other night, I went to check on Max. I watched him sleep. I just can't bear the thought Of what I might be passing on to him.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Besides the physical issues, Are there personal traits You worry about passing on to your children?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: What, Parkinson's isn't enough?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I asked you before, but you didn't answer... How has your relationship been with Max since he arrived? It's been a full week.

dialogue.text: Honestly, I've been worried about him.

dialogue.text: Could that be what you're worried about passing on to Max?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, I hope that he's happier than I am, And healthier. But, you see, you have to understand, That's a major part of it... being sick... The burden I'll be placing on them. Not so easy to be happy when you got that dragging you down.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: dragging me down... that's very similar To how you described yourself in the dream. You feel this weight in your dream Is connected to the Parkinson's.

dialogue.text: I'm being pursued by my father, Overtaken by his illness.

dialogue.text: I'm just... I'm just running. I-I-I... As I said, I feel excited. There's this feeling of, I don't know, possibility. And my father stops me Just like he did in life. As he's doing now with my genetic inheritance.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm struck by the fact that you Become stuck, begin to slow Before you turn and see your father approaching.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: What do you mean, before?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, that's what you said. I'm wondering if you have some agency In stopping yourself from moving forward.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'm slowing down. I'm dragged down. Then I turn and I see It's my father who's doing it.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It angers you when I ask you about your role in this. You were also disturbed by what you take to be Gina's account of you As self-defeating or self sabotaging.

situation: I think I didn't ask for Parkinson's but have it.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Look, any shrink will tell you That a patient is the author of his own life. Of course. Of course that's true. You may now proceed To second-year graduate studies In human psychology. dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you think about what your life might become If you do have Parkinson's?

dialogue.text: I don't know. Probably something very similar To what it held for my father.

situation: I imagine the situation after getting sick.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I don't know. Probably something very similar To what it held for my father. I'd be less and less able to leave the house, Less and less able to take care of myself. Eventually I'd need care In my own home. Then, in the final stages, I'd be lifted up And carried off to a nursing home Still in my fucking chair, given round-the-clock care Like an infant in diapers and a bib.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Is there anything that feels comforting to you

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: In that fantasy? Fantasy? Is that a joke?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: We're not talking about the majority of adult men. We're talking about you.

dialogue.text: Precisely. Why the fuck would I want to have Parkinson's disease?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why on earth would I find that comforting? This is why I should have been more diligent In finding a therapist with a bit of life experience. dialogue.text: You're 57 years old, not 80. You were told this week by a qualified neurologist That you probably don't have Parkinson's...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: He said that we would have to wait and see.

dialogue.text: Okay. I think We're out of time.

dialogue.text: Will you tell me something before we finish? In the beginning of your dream... You described it quite vividly... That excitement, The feeling of openness, possibility. When was the last time you felt that? Can you remember?

dialogue.text: Did you find that disturbing?

situation: I describe my daughter-in-law's way of exercising, and the therapist notes this is the same way I describe TV shows.

dialogue.text: Two nights ago Julia was in her exercise room On the second floor, right? So I was trying to read, But I could not concentrate Because her music was so loud. I could... I could feel it Vibrating through the floor, you know. So I thought I'll go down and ask her If she could please turn the music down a little bit. But I could not bring myself to do this, Paul, Because she was running, bending, dancing, sweating so much That I did not want to embarrass her. Julia was like a desperate animal, Wanting so badly to keep up. She was even punishing herself when she could not. She was yelling, come on, Julia. Julia, come on. Come on, Julia. Julia, come on. So much sweating, So out of breath, you know. Doom-doom doom-doom doom-doom doom-doom... constant. I have never seen her in that state before.

dialogue.text: I suppose you find this amusing.

dialogue.speaker: client

dialogue.text: I do think it's interesting That you described Julia in the same way that you described The female television contestants... Desperate, primal, like crazed animals. problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I described taking my son to a concert and feeling conflicted about his behavior. I struggle with the emotions of watching my son and feeling responsible for his happiness. The therapist acknowledged my role as a father and the difficulty of seeing my son unhappy.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Do you know animal collective?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm gonna assume that's a band.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Max told me last month that he'd missed them When they played in Baltimore Because of his mother and Steve's engagement party. So I saw that they were playing here And I got tickets. dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And Max?

dialogue.text: Max stayed pinned to my side. He went closer when I prodded him, but...

dialogue.text: What?

dialogue.text: You know, he kept coming back to check on me. So I'd send him off again And he'd go stand at the edge of things, Against the side wall, with his hood on. It was... It was just hard for me to watch him.

dialogue.text: This is his favorite band?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You say it was hard for you to watch him. Can you tell me why?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Because I'm his father.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: He's my son.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I discussed my experience of watching someone and the emotional effect it had on me. I also talked about a mistake I made with my computer history.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You're asking me why it was hard for me to see him unhappy. Clearly you haven't had kids.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm asking if you can describe in more detail What it felt like to watch him. You said he kept coming back to check on you. Why do you think that is?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I was deafened by the noise. And... I couldn't help wondering how Sunil... What he would make of all this.

dialogue.text: Sunil? Your patient?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Right.

dialogue.text: Why do you bring him up?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And you think Max somehow picked up on this? That's why he kept coming back to check on you? Surely you weren't the only parent Standing uncomfortably in the back. I... I guess I'm not so clear Why Max would be so concerned. Are you all right? Paul.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I... I made a terrible mistake.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I discussed with the therapist my decision not to tell Max the truth and my desire to protect him in that moment. I reflected on the irony of the situation and the emotional impact it had on me.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I made a terrible mistake.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Tell me.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I let Max use my computer before we left To find the directions to the concert, And I... I didn't realize I hadn't cleared The searches from the list From the... the history. So I walk into the room And he's scrolling through this list of searches, Hundreds of them... Parkinson's institute, Parkinson's disease foundation. I know all of them by heart. And...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I just... I just knew from his face Exactly what he'd seen. And he... Asked me... If I was sick.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What did you say?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I said no.

situation: I deleted records of my illness from my computer.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I said it... that wasn't about me. I was researching for a patient. But Max is... he's exceptionally bright. It's never been easy to lie to him. His sister's seven years older, And he told her there was no tooth fairy.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Did you consider telling him the truth?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I was just in shock. And he was just looking at me With his big eyes. And I thought, he's scared. Get through the moment, get out the door, See the concert. You can ruin his life later, Not like this though. Not right now. I mean, it's fucking crazy... All this time I'm consumed with how best to break it, And then to have it happen like this, In... In the worst possible way.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Was that the entire conversation?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Pretty much. We got home. I put him to bed. And I went to my computer And I just erased the whole history.

dialogue.text: It is worse, having told me?

dialogue.text: I shouldn't have had those drinks. I know that. I don't drink alone. After the night that I had...

situation: I described a dream filled with fear and an unexplained and significant emotion, and that I woke up unable to sleep to see my son and them.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Before I realized what had happened, I was in the backyard of my son's house. And I was digging a hole with my bare hands. And I was digging so desperately and intensely that I could feel my tongue swelling in my mouth. Then I reached to put the animal in the hole, but it was too dark. I could not locate it. And then I realized I had already. I cannot say what it was, but it felt... It felt as if it was very very important to me. And then Arun was... My son... Arun was suddenly approaching. He was coming towards me quickly, and his eyes were enormous. I felt that I had done something terribly wrong. And I woke up. When I woke up, I could still feel the soil under my fingernails. You're quiet. You have no reaction to the dream I just told you?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'd rather hear your reaction.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I could not fall back asleep, so I went down the hall to Arun and Julia's room.

situation: I am disturbed by Julia's peaceful sleep and shared a dream about a declining animal. The therapist explored the possible connections between the dream and my feelings towards Julia and her son.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: My son and his wife sleep turned away from each other, as if they have been thrown from opposite sides of a speeding car. My son's breathing is labored. He snores powerfully. But Julia...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What... what about Julia?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She sleeps so easily, Paul, as if nothing can hurt her. While she keeps this secret from my son, she sleeps with such peace on her face.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Can I ask you how long you were watching them?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Maybe 15 minutes. Then I could not fall back asleep for the rest of the night. And my mind kept returning to the dream.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you mind if we discussed the dream a little bit more?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Do you see terrible omens?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Omens. I simply thought that we could make some associations.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Associations?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Can you... Can you tell me... Can you tell me a little more about the animal that you saw in the dream? You said that you weren't quite sure whether it was a goat or a dog.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes, I only know that it had a dark coat and that it had great difficulty breathing.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Like Arun? You said that his breathing was labored while you watched him sleep.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You think the animal in my dream was Arun?

situation: The therapist explored the symbolism in my dream and its connection to my feelings towards Julia, discussing my sense of time running out and my coping mechanism of smoking.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You think the animal in my dream was Arun?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You said that the animal was in a state of decline. And you also gave it a gender.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Did I?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, when you were standing over this animal with a stick, you called it a her.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: So now you think the animal is Julia?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I don't know. Is that what you think? Did you have the dream the night you found the pills?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah. Yes, you're right.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What else do you think that the dream might indicate?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You want to smoke?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Oh no.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: It's very light.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: No, thank you. You talked about the sense that time was running out, both at the shore and at your son's house, as he was walking towards you. And you referred to this sense of desperation.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Hmm, time. Time, yes. There's never enough... Never.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Time to do what?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: That's the question, isn't it? What is there to do? I find that smoking makes me calm. Cigarettes have this effect on me.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Would you... Would you mind if we continued to talk about the dream?
dialogue.strategy: Guiding the Pace and Depth of the Conversation

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I started smoking when I was in university. Did I tell you that?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, you did. You told me the first day that you came to see me.

situation: I reflected on my past relationship with Malini and the significance of smoking in our interactions. The therapist explored my feelings about the end of that relationship and the societal factors that influenced it.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, I'm pleased to see that you remember the things that I say to you, Paul. You also remember the woman I mentioned to you... Malini?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So you'd rather talk about Malini?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: In my final year, I followed her out of the library. I... I watched her light a cigarette. I thought to myself, I must learn to smoke so that I can talk to her.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I suppose there are worse reasons people start to smoke.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: One afternoon we went to watch Satyajit Ray's film. Afterwards we went to a cafe, then we smoked cigarettes, then we discussed the theme of the movie. And I thought I was being so sophisticated. And Malini smoked with such ease. And you must know one thing... in those days it was extremely rare for a woman to smoke outside. And the look on her face when she drew the smoke into her lungs... It was like as if she knew some great secret. And I smoked like my eyelashes were on fire. I could watch her smoke all day... All day.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Last week you mentioned that the relationship between you and Malini had to end.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes, this is true. What is the American phrase... All good things must end badly?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: All good things must come to an end. But it's kind of interesting the way you phrase it. Did things end badly?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I was Brahmin. She was not. I was from a different caste.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So she was from a lower caste than yours.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: The caste system was established to keep the societal order.

situation: I opened up about my past relationship with Malini, sharing the intense emotions I felt and the pain I experienced when she ended the relationship.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I was an only child... An only son of my family. And I knew they were not going to approve.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And did you know she was from another caste when you met her?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Of course. But it made no difference. I... I could not resist her. I wanted to spend each and every moment of my life with her. We studied together. We took walks together. We went to the cinema. And sometimes we did nothing, but that was okay too.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Mm-hmm. So were you... Were you intimate? Sunil?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I should not have been.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Why not?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Perhaps we should continue discussing my dream.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, we can, but I would like you to tell me what happened with Malini first.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She ended our relationship.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: She did? And how did she end the relationship?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She... She...

situation: I told about my past relationship with Malini and how sad I was to break up with her.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I agreed to meet her on the steps of the library. So I thought she was going to surprise me with a gift or a note or... But she told me she could no longer see me. I pleaded with her to reconsider, but we had a terrible argument and she walked away wearing my coat. I felt like someone was pulling a spool of hot thread through my heart. And that was the last time I ever saw her.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: But, Sunil, I have to point out that this contradicts what you told me during the last session. Last week when you were talking about Malini, you said that you had made a great sacrifice. You said that you hadn't got any patience for people who put their desires before their principles. But now it seems that the choice was not yours to make. Did you ever make any attempt to contact her again after she walked away?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why are you so interested in Malini?

situation: I talked about my ex-girlfriend’s suicide after she broke up with her.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why does she fascinate you? Leave her. Let her go.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Because when you talk about her, I see a side of you that I haven't seen before.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No, it's not really there, Paul. This side of me, as you say, it's... You're talking to a ghost.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I don't think that's true. I think the part of you that loved Malini is deeply hidden. Why do you say a ghost? Sunil?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: There's a bridge in Calcutta. It's called the Howrah bridge.

situation: The therapist offered condolences for my pain and acknowledged my reluctance to discuss the topic. I shared that I never spoke about it except during the police investigation and eventually moved on by marrying someone else.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: There's a bridge in Calcutta. It's called the Howrah bridge. It spans the Hooghly river, which links Howrah city and Calcutta. My family was from the other side. She threw herself from the bridge and drowned. When they found her body at the bottom of the river, she was still wearing the same jacket... When she left. I don't know why. Yeah, I know. There were heavy stones in her pockets... In the pockets of the jacket.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm... I'm so very sorry.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why are you sorry? You didn't know her.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I'm sorry for you.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: For the pain that you experienced; for the pain that you still carry with you.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: The pain that I still carry?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I... I didn't realize that... That she'd killed herself. You told me the last time that you'd never spoken about this to anybody.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No. The police spoke to me. There was a brief investigation.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: An investigation?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: They knew Malini and I spent time together. My mother had stitched my name into the lining of my jacket. Hmm.

situation: I was very sad after my ex-girlfriend died. The police came to investigate, and I lived with pain for 32 years. The therapist believed that the poor relationship between me and Julia was related to this experience.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: They were curious like you. But nothing came out of the investigation. A few months later I graduated with honors. Kamala and I were married soon after.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So you've had to live with this... This awful tragedy privately for the past 30 years?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: 32 years, actually. But it's nothing. It's simply a scar.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It's more than just a scar. Malini was obviously somebody that you were deeply connected to. She ended the relationship and she took her own life. Just to go back to the dream for a moment... You said that the animal fell from a high cliff. And Malini fell to her death from a bridge.
dialogue.strategy: Guiding the Pace and Depth of the Conversation

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: When you talk about Malini and the passion of your relationship, it reminds me of how you described your son and Julia when they first came to visit you in Calcutta.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See, Paul, please please don't compare my relationship with Malini to Arun and Julia. Listen, this is preposterous.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: With all due respect, Sunil, I don't think it is. You said that you never talked about Malini with anybody since the police investigation. Now here you are, talking to me 32 years later. I don't think that's a coincidence. But I think maybe something in the way that Julia and Arun relate to each other... The intimacy with which they relate... Reminds you of your own intimacy with Malini. And that perhaps... Perhaps that may be one of the reasons why you feel so conflicted in your relationship to your daughter-in-law.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: ( Sighs ) Maybe.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I shared my difficulty living with Julia and the therapist offered understanding and help.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Maybe, Paul. I don't know. But what I do know without question is it is more and more difficult for me to live in the presence of Julia, to continue living in her... In her house.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yeah, I understand. Well, is there anything that we can discuss that might improve that situation?
dialogue.strategy: Guiding the Pace and Depth of the Conversation

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: See, I have already told you there's... There's nothing to be done. I have no options.

situation: I have to go home, before julia realizes that I took her birth control pill, the therapist thinks that I am facing a problem recently, and I can call him at any time if needed.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I must go now.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: There's... there's still a little time left.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I have to return these pills, you know, before she notices.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You've obviously been through a lot in the last... In the last week... Finding these pills, the intensity of your dream. If these emotions have stirred anything that makes you feel overwhelmed...

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: What does that mean?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I mean, if you're continuing to have trouble sleeping, for example, or if you have disturbing thoughts or any more of these dreams that keep you awake, I just want you to know that you can call me. And perhaps after you return these pills in Julia's drawer, you should think about not going into her study again.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Goodbye. Thank you. Thank you.

situation: I discussed my new haircut for a play, my therapist asked me if I still forgot my words, and last week I was worried about making a mistake on stage.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You cut your hair. It's different. It's lighter.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Darker, for the play.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It's very... very becoming.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, it's becoming Maxine, not me. You know, I look in the mirror, wear the shirt. It helps me to find her reality. Not that that reality is all that different than my reality, but...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She's recently widowed, all alone in the world, sex-starved. You know, I am... Well, there are overlaps.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Overlaps? Do you think that has anything to do with why you might be struggling with your lines?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Maybe.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: So how... how did the week go?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Fine.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Any lapses?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Not really.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You left here last week and you were terrified that you were going to fail in front of the audience in the theater.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah well, there are still moments when I'm onstage that I worry about stumbling on this scene or that, but I manage. I get through.

situation: The therapist asked me why I was angry and how I felt when I left last week, and I said it had something to do with his rejection last week and my comment on the lines.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah well, there are still moments when I'm onstage that I worry about stumbling on this scene or that, but I manage. I get through.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Is one of those scenes the one you asked me to read with you last week? You were pretty angry when you left.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No, I understood why you kicked me out.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Kicked you out?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, it was inappropriate. You were not comfortable.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, that's... that's true. But the way I remember it, you stormed out of the room. How do you remember that moment?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I asked you to run lines and you refused to help me. I felt sorry for you.
dialogue.fine_label: A1 争辩-挑战  A2 争�

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Really?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, I mean it must be strange, you know, treating someone like me.

situation: The therapist asked me if I was happy at work and wanted to know about my experience and feelings about the exercise.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, I mean it must be strange, you know, treating someone like me.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You mean somebody famous like you.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You know, ultimately it's not that interesting to read a scene, so...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Is that something that you've been feeling... that your work isn't that interesting? Because you have spoken about it passionately in the past.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah well, there are times.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Would you like to talk about one of these times?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, it's just that I would... I'd like to understand what it is that you are experiencing, what you're feeling. I've never done it, so I'm curious.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Well, you know I felt really disconnected all that time in rehearsal.

situation: I talked about how I felt during rehearsals that week, and the therapist asked about how I felt and helped me analyze how I felt during the performance.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: And this week... this week in previews, I really felt like I understood something new about what I... what she needed, you know, in a moment. And it just clicked into place. It was... Well, I was totally in time... Present. Maybe it was just the haircut.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And this feeling of feeling present... Was it momentary?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No, it lasted till the end. And it was palpable. I mean, the applause was...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Loud.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: That must have felt good. Think of where you were. You were terrified. You were dreading the week of previews. Then the play goes on. It's a success. You make this connection. You must feel a satisfaction. What happens between then and now?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I go home. The apartment's dark. The fridge is empty. I open a can of soup. It's a nasty hangover... my life.

situation: I invited my therapist to my opening night and the therapist asked why but declined because it would interfere with the effectiveness of the therapy.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Do you want to come to opening night? I have a set of tickets and I was just thinking, you know, why don't you just come?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Why would you want me there?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I don't know. You sound interested, so...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Any other reasons?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You could see that I'm good.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, I know that.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Why?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Because I've seen your films.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Which ones?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: All of them.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Anyway, you've never seen me onstage, right?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: No, I ve not seen you onstage.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: So there you go. You could come and see what it is that I do. I mean, is that so strange? You just said you wanted to...

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It's not strange at all. But I'm gonna have to say no.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Okay, well, is that because of me or some policy or...?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well yes, it is a kind of policy. I think that... I think that it would interfere with the work that we're trying to do here in this room. But please don't take that personally.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No, that's fine. I understand. I'll sell them on ebay. ( Chuckles )

situation: The therapist took the initiative to ask me if I had invited Patricia to the show and if I had communicated with her. I replied that I had apologized, but she did not remember it. I felt very embarrassed.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You were considering inviting Patricia. Did you do that? Why not? Have you spoken to Patricia this week?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I did what you told me to do.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What did I tell you to do?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You told me that it wasn't too late to make amends. So I went to her and I apologized.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: For telling her not to be an actress.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She didn't even know what I was talking about. She hardly remembered being in that play. You know, I told her that I thought she was wonderful and that it was wrong of me to dissuade her. And she said, oh, don't worry about that. And then she thanked me. She said, I don't know how you bear all that bullshit. She said I saved her. And then... this is this best... she said, I'm glad I got to lead a real life. A real life... can you believe that?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: It must have been hurtful.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: You think? Humiliating. I mean, I was trying to apologize.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And did you tell her that? That it felt painful?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Of course not.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And can I ask why?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She's sick, Paul.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: My sister was sick and I went to her to find out what she thought about life. The therapy was to ask me how I viewed life and show that I cared about other people's opinions.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She's sick, Paul. I went there to make amends, not pick a fight.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I... I... I wajust aware that you felt guilty. I thought that talking to Patricia might be helpful. I'm sorry it wasn't.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: At least now I know what she thinks of me, what she thinks of the life I chose.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What do you think of the life you chose? The last time we spoke I had the feeling that you are very invested in the way other people see you and your sister's judgment has... It's clearly had a big impact on how you view yourself.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Look, you know, I understand that tricia wouldn't want my life anyway.

situation: The therapist told me why I thought I had a spiritual connection with Russell when I met him. I said that I imagined them to prove myself.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: All my conctions are, you know, fiction. Maybe they always have been.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Do you really believe that? I mean, when you met Russell, you told me that you had a really deep connection with him.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah well, I think we did at first. I just... I always felt like I had to prove myself to Russell.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Prove yourself?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, to Russell and his friends... You know, these academics, shrinks, political scientists. I always thought they were gonna see right through me.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: And what do you think they would see?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: That there's no there there. That's what Russell used to say about L.A.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: You were afraid that that's how Russell saw you, and his friends... no there there.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, Russell's shallow actress wife.

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: The therapist encouraged me to ask someone else to accompany me, while I expressed my addiction to reading my daughter's emails. I dismissed my daughter's compliment and struggled with self-worth.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah, Russell's shallow actress wife. Oh, but how the fuck would they know? They've never come to a performance either.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Are you upset with me because I said I wouldn't come to your play? You invited me to an important event... Your opening night. And I thank you for that. But isn't there somebody else you'd like to ask instead? We talked about tricia. What about izzy? Isn't she someone you'd like to take with you? Have you thought about asking her?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: No, that would require us to be in the same building.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Well, surely you know that the relationship with izzy will survive this teenage angst.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I'm not sure about that.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: I know it may not feel that way, but... You know, sometimes I think that having a teenager is like going to the dark side of the moon. The person that you know and that you love just disappears. And you just have to trust that eventually they will come back. Maybe different, but they will come back.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Did that happen to you?

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Yes, with my daughter, yes. Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Yeah well, I'm still reading my daughter's emails, so... ( Chuckles )

problem_type: The relationship with friends and family
situation: I secretly read my daughter's emails and observed her life. My daughter praised me for my acting skills. The therapist asked me what I thought of my daughter's evaluation of me, thinking that I was denying my own value.

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: I don't know. It's an addiction, you know? Like a junkie just waiting for hits of information about my own kid. You know, she signs some of them Isabel now. I mean, when did she become Isabel? You might be curious to know that her and young Miller have not yet had sex. They talk about it, however, all the time. I kind of want to tell her, try to preserve some of the mystery. But I want to tell her a lot of things. ( Sighs ) She did say something nice. Miller had seen a movie of mine on tv and he said, your mother was amazing. And izzy wrote back, she is amazing.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: Were you surprised by that comment?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: Oh, it was a silly movie. I got good enough revws, but it wasn't my best work.

dialogue.speaker: therapist
dialogue.text: What I meant was, were you surprised that izzy would compliment you like that?

dialogue.speaker: client
dialogue.text: She wasn't speaking of me. She was speaking of the performance.
